system.name: Hydra
system.one_liner: a distributed massive MIMO uplink baseband-processing architecture that reduces cross-server data shuffles versus BigStation by co-locating ZF, equalization, and demodulation

components.name: RU antennas
components.role: source of per-antenna IQ samples feeding the pipeline (time-domain in BigStation, frequency-domain in Hydra)

components.name: FFT
components.role: per-antenna stage that runs before the first cross-server data shuffle

components.name: ZF
components.role: zero-forcing equalization stage run on commodity servers after antennas are shuffled to subcarrier-parallel layout

components.name: Equal & Demod
components.role: combined equalization and demodulation stage in BigStation, reached and left via a separate data shuffle

components.name: Equal
components.role: equalization stage in Hydra, grouped with ZF and Demod inside one dashed box with no intervening shuffle

components.name: Demod
components.role: demodulation stage in Hydra, grouped with ZF and Equal so no shuffle separates them

components.name: Decode
components.role: LDPC decoding stage, the final pipeline step in both architectures

flows.what: all-to-all shuffled data moving from antenna-parallel to subcarrier-parallel layout
data passed within the same dashed group with no shuffle (Hydra architecture only)

content.key_idea: Hydra cuts the number of network data shuffles versus BigStation by co-locating ZF, equalization, and demodulation on the same commodity server, shuffling only before and after that combined stage.
content.reading_order: Top panel (a) BigStation and bottom panel (b) Hydra each read left to right: antennas through FFT into ZF, Equal/Demod, and Decode via crossing shuffle lines.

palette.used_for: fill of all pipeline-stage boxes (FFT, ZF, Equal & Demod, Decode)
text labels, box outlines, dashed grouping box, and shuffle arrows

style.stroke: thin black rules (~0.6pt) solid on stage boxes, dashed for the Hydra grouping box and panel divider
style.font: Arial-like sans (with some Linux Libertine text), roughly 5.5-6.5pt labels, not bold
style.arrows: straight black lines with arrowheads crossing in an all-to-all crossbar pattern between successive pipeline stages

encoding.line_style_means: solid lines trace the per-antenna to per-subcarrier data path through FFT/ZF/Equal/Demod/Decode; the dashed rectangle in the Hydra panel groups ZF, Equal, and Demod as co-located with no intervening shuffle
encoding.emphasis: the dashed box around ZF/Equal/Demod in the Hydra panel is the sole visual marker distinguishing it from BigStation's fully-shuffled pipeline
reusable_patterns: crossbar of crossing lines depicting an all-to-all data shuffle between pipeline stages

no labels quantifying how many shuffles are saved

evidence: Unlike BigStation, Hydra shuffles data only after the subcarrier-parallel stage.
BigStation is the state-of-the-art design for virtualized distributed massive MIMO baseband processing.

summary: This figure compares two distributed massive MIMO uplink baseband-processing pipelines: BigStation, the prior state-of-the-art design, and Hydra, the architecture used in this work. Both pipelines run per-antenna IQ samples through FFT, zero-forcing (ZF) equalization, equalization-and-demodulation, and LDPC decoding stages on commodity servers, with crossing lines depicting the all-to-all data shuffle needed between antenna-parallel and subcarrier-parallel stages. In BigStation (a), FFT takes time-domain samples and each of ZF, Equal & Demod, and Decode is separated by its own shuffle. In Hydra (b), FFT takes frequency-domain samples, and a dashed box groups ZF, Equal, and Demod so they run without an intervening shuffle, leaving only one shuffle before this group and one before Decode. The figure is plain black-and-white boxes and crossing arrows with no color coding; only labels and the dashed grouping box distinguish the two designs.
summary_zh: 该图对比两种分布式大规模MIMO上行基带处理架构：BigStation与Hydra。二者均经FFT、ZF均衡、解调、LDPC译码等阶段，箭头交叉表示数据洗牌；Hydra用虚线框将ZF、均衡、解调归入同一商用服务器，减少了洗牌次数。
notes: System name 'Hydra' is inferred from the caption's contrast with the prior state-of-the-art BigStation; the supplied paragraph is truncated right after introducing BigStation's limitations, so no further text on Hydra's rationale is available beyond the caption.
